text:
jordan: quick sanity check — Go client started returning 401 on /v1/generate after I wired REDWOOD_API_KEY into a systemd EnvironmentFile. No code changes. Anyone seen this?

jordan: here's how I load it in the unit file:
```
[Service]
EnvironmentFile=/etc/myapp/env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/myapp
```
and /etc/myapp/env contains:
```
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_ABC123...

```

alex: two quick things to rule out: 1) systemd keeps the newline, 2) you're using the right auth scheme. Our hosted API expects Bearer tokens (Authorization: Bearer <key>) — some old scripts used Basic with username `api` which is different.

alex: check raw header with curl locally to see if key is intact:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```

maya: also run `xxd` or `od -c` to see hidden chars in the file. trailing \r or NUL will make the header mismatched. e.g.:
```
$ od -c /etc/myapp/env | sed -n '1p'
0000000   R   E   D   W   O   O   D   _   A   P   I   _   K   E   Y   =
0000020   s   k   _   l   i   v   e   _   A   B   C   1   2   3  \r  \n
0000040
```

jordan: oh nice — the od output shows a \r before the \n. I had created the file on Windows and scp'd it over.

alex: easiest quick fix: strip CR and reload unit: `tr -d '\r' < /etc/myapp/env > /etc/myapp/env.clean && mv /etc/myapp/env.clean /etc/myapp/env && systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart myapp`

maya: alternative: set Environment in the unit directly (safer for secrets):
```
Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_ABC123...
```
but remember unit files are world-readable unless you protect them.

jordan: fixed it by `dos2unix /etc/myapp/env` and restart — now 200 on the health endpoint. thanks! :tada:

devex-bot: docs: https://docs.redwood.com/docs/authentication#api-keys (note: prefer Bearer header; Basic auth only for legacy integrations)

maya: small follow-up — if anyone hits streaming 401s, also check client timeout/retries: some proxies strip headers on 100-continue flow. ping me and I can share a small proxy test script.

jordan: will do, thanks all :thumbsup:
